an operator-forced sweep outside the night

emits.because: a stamped turn carrying hop.session_id, for the context assembly
a finished session carrying hop.session_id, hop.channel and hop.audience_set -- the id, the room and the round it was spoken to

a step of this keeper that the session store did not answer (GH #343). hop.reject_reason is 'store_refused', hop.store_error carries the store's own error_code -- a free string, because the store's code list is open -- and hop.store_operation the refused op. The body names the STEP that was refused, because they do not leave the same thing standing -- at 'touch' and 'open' the stamped turn has ALREADY left in the same emission, and at 'open' the missing row makes the next turn open yet another generation. It matters because every one of these failures reads as a correct run: an unanswered lookup looks like a channel with no open session (and used to OPEN a second generation for one that had one), and an unanswered nightly sweep looks like a night with no idle channel. Drain it: undrained, a keeper that stopped keeping is indistinguishable from a quiet one

description.purpose: Scope marker of the session keeper: bundles the channel-generation state and the two passes that move it — the stamp in the ingress path and the nightly close. THE HIVE IS THE ADDRESS: a caller sends to the keeper and names a lane, never a cell inside it. A session is a phone call on a channel: it begins with a turn, it ends deterministically, and everything downstream only reads the id.
description.use_when: One per agent surface, in front of the context assembly. Wire the parent's edges TO THE HIVE PATH — see meclaw-overview § Die Hive-Grenze. `params.ports` is empty and therefore sealed: a mutation reaching inside is rejected with hive_port_boundary. The keeper is an island until an edge crosses into it.
description.not_in_scope: No conversation content and no context assembly -- the turns live in the collector's window. No judgement about whether a conversation is over: the close is a timer plus an idle threshold, never a model call. Nothing is deleted; a closed generation stays as a row. And no roster: the round of a generation is recorded once, when the generation opens, and never rewritten (ADR-0002 E12).
description.contract_in: in_turn — an inbound turn from the surface; the caller MUST promote the channel identity to context.channel, or every chat lands on the channel 'default', and SHOULD promote the round to context.audience_set, or the generation this turn opens records none. in_sweep — an operator-forced sweep outside the night. Any other route is refused by the hive rather than delivered to a cell that would not know it.
description.contract_out: turn — a stamped turn, carrying hop.session_id, for the context assembly (promote the id to context on that edge; that IS the stamp). close — a finished session, carrying hop.session_id, hop.channel and hop.audience_set, for whoever consumes one (the collector's in_close lane). The close is fired by a TIMER, which has no context of its own: everything it says about the round comes off the generation row, so the consuming edge has all three keys to promote and none of them is guessed.
